findings.title: The wallet's every-transaction Blaster families have no Falsified control: 307 Valid theorems with nothing that would flag a vacuous Valid
findings.scenario: Blaster's SMT background for one of these goals is contradictory. That is Lean-blaster #194's false-Valid class, which the audit (blaster-unguarded-axioms-unmeasured) found unfixed at this pin and measured only for the scenario modules. The theorem then prints ✅ Valid whatever the bytes do: for example, wallet_any_tx_fails_without_the_signer stays Valid on a wallet whose list.has check is gone. Nothing in the tree would show it. These modules have no `solve-result: 1` control: AlwaysFalseAnyTx (1), WalletPurposeAnyTx (5), WalletNoLockAnyTx (18), WalletRedeemerAnyTx (22), WalletAnyTx, Two and Three (13), and Signers4 to Signers127 (248). Audit/ has none for them either, and Audit/diag doesn't list them. The policy's every-transaction families each carry a cut control and Slice/ carries six, so the same failure there would print '❌ Unexpected Valid' and fail the build. Only Signers128 has one on the wallet side (Control128). No funds are at stake: the claim rests on the kernel's Seedelf.Every.wallet_accepts_iff. What's weakened is the 'cross-check by another route' that CLAIMS.md and the README cite these modules for.
findings.evidence:
`grep -rn "solve-result: 1" Seedelf/*.lean Seedelf/Signers/Control128.lean Slice/Slice/*.lean` finds controls only at:
- PolicyRedeemerAnyTx.lean:60
- PolicyPurposeAnyTx.lean:64
- PolicyLinesFourAnyTx.lean:119
- PolicyLinesFiveAnyTx.lean:207
- PolicyLinesAnyTx.lean:130
- Signers/Control128.lean:126 and :162
- Slice/Slice/Controls.lean:51, 58, 65, 72, 99, 111

That is 7 plus 6, matching chunk 42's record of '7 controls Falsified, plus Slice's ... 6'.

The theorems with no twin:
- AlwaysFalseAnyTx.lean:111
- WalletPurposeAnyTx.lean:158-162
- WalletNoLockAnyTx.lean:71-88
- WalletRedeemerAnyTx.lean:182-203
- WalletAnyTx.lean:43-69
- WalletAnyTxTwo.lean:98-116
- WalletAnyTxThree.lean:144-162
- Signers{4..127}.lean (2 theorems each; a mechanical check of all 125 Signers modules found no control in any of them)

In Audit/, `grep -rln "AnyTx\|appliedAnyTx\|appliedSig" Audit/` returns nothing. Audit/diag/list-all.txt holds the wallet's scenario theorems only (D276 always_false_always_fails, D304-D309 wallet_fails_*, wallet_register_spend_iff).

The policy side shows the pattern this family lacks, at PolicyPurposeAnyTx.lean:61-65: `#prep_uplc appliedPolSpendingCut seedelf polSpendingArgs 155`, two #guards (stillRunning at 155, endsInError at 156), then the theorem restated with `(solve-result: 1)`.

At the pin, Blaster's Env.lean:58-60 logs '❌ Unexpected Valid' as an error for a control expected Falsified, so a control would fail the build on a vacuous background. In tactic mode, Tactic.lean:55-58 closes a Valid goal with `blasterProven` and nothing else.
findings.fix:
Give each wallet family the controls the policy's families carry, in the same module:
- **A cut control.** `#prep_uplc …Cut` one step short of the family's longest concrete run (always_false 99; minting purpose 162; NoLock's Constr 0 [B,B,B] 596; for WalletAnyTx with one signer, 1305, one short of the miss at 1236 + 70k). Add the two guards (stillRunning, endsInError or endsWithUnit) and the theorem restated with `(gen-cex: 0) (solve-result: 1)`.
- **A spec mutant for the iffs.** Drop `vkh = signer`, or drop `schnorrAccepts … = true`.
- **A flip for NoLock.** Audit NL2's form: not every Register spend returns unit.

For Signers, have gen-seedelf-signers.py emit Control128's two controls at a few lengths (4, 64, 127) or at every k.

Add one theorem per family to Audit/diag's lists, for the #194 replay.

The same class sits in Lovejoin/AnyTx (V4b's lane). How much build time to spend here turns on chunk 49's open call 6 (keep or retire the Blaster Seedelf modules).

findings.title: PolicyLinesAnyTx's header says mints of six lines or more 'aren't proved', though PolicyLinesAll proves every length in the kernel
findings.scenario: Someone reading the Blaster lines family's header learns that a mint of six or more lines is outside every proof. PolicyLinesAll.policy_fails_two_or_more_lines and LinesAllAnyMint.policy_fails_unless_one_line prove every length in the kernel. Both came in the same commit, and the README's table cites them for exactly this. The sentence was true only of the Blaster modules.
findings.evidence:
PolicyLinesAnyTx.lean:21-23: "Four lines are PolicyLinesFourAnyTx and five PolicyLinesFiveAnyTx; six and more aren't proved, since the ledger bounds a mint's lines only by the transaction's size and budget." Against that:
- PolicyLinesAll.lean:81-86: `theorem policy_fails_two_or_more_lines : ∀ … lines, 2 ≤ lineCount lines → ∃ n, cekExecuteProgram seedelf.script … n = State.Error`, kernel-checked.
- README's table row: 'PolicyLinesAll, LinesAllAnyMint | A mint of two lines or more fails, at every length'.
findings.fix: Reword to "six and more aren't proved by Blaster; PolicyLinesAll and LinesAllAnyMint prove every length in the kernel".
findings.known_check: I checked the audit's stale-seedelf-module-docs targets (Policy.lean:4-8, WalletNoLock.lean:8-10, WalletPurpose.lean:4-6, Wallet.lean). This line isn't among them, and the audit predates the module. docs/backlog.md and the archived plans have no mention of it.

checked_ok:
At the pin (PlutusCoreBlaster 68c5399), a run cut short by the step limit can't make a theorem hold:
- `isUnsuccessful` is `isErrorState` and `isSuccessful` is `isHaltState` (UPLC/Utils.lean:26-41).
- `cekExecuteProgram` runs `runStepsPreservingState`, which returns the Eval/Return state when fuel runs out (CekMachine.lean). An exhausted run is neither.
- So no failure theorem in the lane holds because a run was cut short, and every success theorem needs a halt inside its limit.

`#prep_uplc` (PreProcess.lean) defines `NAME.exec` as `cekExecuteProgram script (args xs) N` and `NAME.prop` as Blaster's optimized rewrite of it. Every AnyTx, Signers and PolicyLines module #guards its builder's `.exec` at its own limit, passing and failing.

I reran gen-seedelf-signers.py and gen-seedelf-slice.py from a scratch copy. Their output is byte-identical to the tree: Signers/*, Signers.lean, modules.txt, Index0-3 and Rule.lean. Only Control128 is hand-written, as its doc says.
Slice/: Index0-3 prove RuleAt k for each k in 0..255 exactly once. Rule's match maps all 256 to the right theorem, and the off-byte theorems close the rest of Int, kernel-combined.

Slice/Common's 14 copied definitions are byte-identical to the main package's (ofHex, TxRest, infoWith, returnsUnit, endsWithUnit, endsInError, endOf, seedelfPrefix, exampleTxid, seedelfName, mintIn, withMint, inputsFrom, oneLine). So sliceRuleArgs is exactly PolicyShapes' fourth disjunct.

The Slice pin 96261cc differs from 68c5399 only by `opaque sliceByteStringOpaque (s k : Int) (bs : String)`, wrapping PLC.sliceByteString (read with git diff in blaster-forks/PlutusCoreBlaster-slice). policyAccepts calls it exactly as the builtin does: start, length, bytes, with lengths 4, 15 and 32.

PolicyShapes' hypotheses aren't vacuous. CardanoLedgerApiBlaster's validMintValue and validInputs (9938562) hold for real one-line mints and non-empty inputs, and the cover theorem takes the two directly.
The README's theorem counts for the lane's rows match the modules: 13+250, 10, 15, 31, 15, 5, 4, 22, 18, 5, 1, and Slice's 258.

The 128-signatory bound holds. Each signatory costs a 30-byte hash plus a 101-byte vkey witness, 131 bytes, so a 16,384-byte transaction carries at most 125. seedelf-core's spends carry one or two (build.rs:2193-2194).
Control128's two controls are meaningful: the 128th disjunct dropped, and unit-or-error at one step short of the miss. Both are guarded concretely at 10195 and 11460.
Slice controls C1-C6 target the byte bound, the burn prefix (dropped, and length 3), pid = own, and both step limits (1286/1287 mint, 1114/1115 off-byte burn).
No `axiom`, `sorry` or `native_decide` is declared in any lane file.

Blaster in tactic mode leaves an Undetermined goal unsolved, so the build fails. `#blaster` with solve-result 1 errors on Valid and only warns on Undetermined, which check.sh counts as UNDETERM (Env.lean:55-70, Tactic.lean:48-63).

seedelfName (Policy.lean:159) matches token_name.generate at 5b82530: push = cons idx, slice(0,14) = 15 bytes, slice(0,31) = 32 bytes, concat order prefix ‖ tag ‖ indexed. The kernel's policyAccepts uses it (Every/PolicyTyped.lean:77).
schnorrAccepts (Wallet.lean:111) calls the builtins in schnorr.ak's order: scalarMul(z, G), add(R, scalarMul(c, U)), equal(g_z, …), blake2b_224(g ‖ g_r ‖ u ‖ vkh). q is BLS12-381's scalar order.

The kernel's headline theorems reuse lane lemmas: exec_error_of_ev, exec_halt_of_ev and exec_never_halts (LinesAllCek), flatten_apply_any, flatPairs and mem_flatPairs (LinesAllAnyMint), and policyBody. Every/Typed.lean:222 and PolicyTyped.lean:235 pin their axioms with #guard_msgs. The stepN lemmas they rest on (CekMachine/Lemmas.lean) read as their names say.

Every top-level Seedelf/*.lean module, and every Slice module, sits in a check.sh family (default, seedelf-any-tx, seedelf-policy-any-tx, seedelf-signers via modules.txt, seedelf-every, seedelf-slice via Slice/modules.txt).
notes: **Settled class, new modules: theorems over the optimizer's output.** The audit's statements-over-optimizer-output was closed by *Exec modules for the scenario suites only. The wallet AnyTx families, Signers and PolicyLines*AnyTx state their theorems over `NAME.prop` alone, with concrete #guards on `NAME.exec` but no exec restatement. None is in Audit/diag's #194 replay lists. Slice/ avoids the gap: its theorems are stated over cekExecuteProgram directly.

**Settled class (print-axioms-check): no axiom guards on these.** PolicyLinesAll, LinesAllAnyMint, LinesAllLoops, PolicyLinesAnyTx's cover (minting_context_layout) and Slice/Rule end in bare `#print axioms`, with no `#guard_msgs`.
- AnyTxShapes, PolicyShapes and Every guard theirs.
- AnyTxCover and PolicyAnyTx have no #print axioms at all, though the README says 'Their #print axioms lists Lean's own alone'.
- No sorry is in the lane today, and Every's guards would catch one in the shared lemmas. But chunk 46's re-pin must rework LinesAllCek's exec lemmas, and a sorry left in PolicyLinesAll's own theorems would pass check.sh as `ok`.
- Cheap fix: #guard_msgs in AnyTxShapes' style. The Blaster cross-checks could guard `[blasterProven, …]` to rule out sorryAx.

**Slice/Controls doesn't vary every check.** No control touches the mint's name check, the amount checks (1 == amt, amt == -1) or the tag's slice length 15. The iff itself pins each one, so this only affects the evidence against a vacuous Valid. C4 drops pid = own from both blocks at once.
**Slice/ isn't in the default run.** Slice/ (seedelf-slice) is one of the Blaster cross-checks CLAIMS.md names, but `./check.sh` alone doesn't run it. The README's full command line does. For V5.

**How I checked without building.** I read the Slice pin's source (96261cc) in /home/logic/Documents/LogicalMechanism/blaster-forks/PlutusCoreBlaster-slice, read-only with git diff, because TREE has no Slice/.lake. The generator reruns wrote only to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-logic-Documents-LogicalMechanism-Seedelf-Wallet/0e0d3674-7c6c-46fb-8cae-a49695fa3bfe/scratchpad/r51/work/V4a/regen/. The checker scripts are v4a_check_signers.py, v4a_check_lines.py and v4a_diff_copies.py in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-logic-Documents-LogicalMechanism-Seedelf-Wallet/0e0d3674-7c6c-46fb-8cae-a49695fa3bfe/scratchpad/r51/work/V4a/.
